program_name: Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management. This is the exact official English name used on unibz.it, in the 2026/27 admission-information PDF, in the brochure and on both signed ranking-list decrees. German: 'Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management' (the name is not translated); the Italian and Ladin versions of the site carry the same English name and the Italian page redirects to a notice reading 'This page is only available in English'. There are two internal study-plan variants whose names appear on sub-pages: 'Study Plan - Data Analytics for Economics' and 'Study Plan - Business Analytics'. Beware of two near-identical unibz programmes that must not be confused with this one: the Master in Computing for Data Science (Faculty of Engineering, LM-18, NOI Techpark) and the discontinued Master in Computational Data Science. Note also that unibz's own ranking-list filename for the Early Bird session misspells the programme: 'Ranking-List-Master-in-Data-Analytics-for-Economics-and-Managment-Early-Bird-Session.pdf' (Managment, missing 'e').
level: master (Italian laurea magistrale, second-cycle). Two years, four semesters, 120 ECTS, entirely in English. Entry qualification is a three-year first-cycle degree (180 ECTS). Programme director: Prof. F. Marta L. Di Lascio (the programme page writes 'Prof. Marta di Lascio'; the ranking-list decrees sign as 'Prof. F. Marta L. Di Lascio'). Student representative in the Course Council: Franz Antonius Bittl. Home faculty: Faculty of Economics and Management (Secretariat +39 0471 013000, schoolofeconomics@unibz.it), but the programme is ALSO listed in the Faculty of Engineering's own study-programme menu and under 'Faculty of Engineering' on the Additional Application Session page — in both places the link resolves to the same Economics-faculty URL, so this is a genuine cross-listing of an inter-faculty programme rather than a second, separate degree.
teaching_language: FULLY ENGLISH — 100%, with no Italian or German component and no language-position system. The admission-information PDF and the programme page both state, verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English.' The brochure 'At a glance' box says 'Courses will be taught in: English'. Every course in both tracks is delivered in English, including the thesis. There is no embedded Italian or German course in the study plan, no first/second/third-language structure, and no trilingual requirement of any kind. This is the decisive structural difference from unibz's trilingual bachelor programmes (and from trilingual masters such as Public Policy and Innovative Governance), which demand C1 + B2 on admission and are effectively closed to English-only applicants. The only language obligation attached to this master is a single English entry level of B2.
campus: Bozen-Bolzano — the main city-centre campus at Universitätsplatz 1 / piazza Università 1, 39100 Bozen-Bolzano (South Tyrol, northern Italy). The brochure 'At a glance' box states plainly 'Campus: Bozen-Bolzano', with no secondary site named. This is the same building that houses the Advisory Service and the Faculty of Economics and Management Secretariat. Note the contrast with the sister data programme, Master in Computing for Data Science, which is taught at the separate NOI Techpark campus (via Bruno Buozzi 1) — despite this programme also being cross-listed by the Faculty of Engineering, its published campus is the city-centre Bolzano campus only. No teaching is scheduled at Brixen-Bressanone, Bruneck-Brunico, Trento or Innsbruck. Emergency/campus service number for Bozen-Bolzano city centre and NOI Techpark: +39 0471 011011.
degree_class: LM-Data (Data Science) — stated as 'Italian degree class: LM-Data' in the 'At a glance' box on both the programme page and the brochure, and confirmed by unibz's own Study Guide, which lists 'Data Analytics for Economics and Management (LM-Data)' alongside the faculty's LM-77 and LM-63 masters. 120 ECTS over 2 years. LM-DATA is one of the newer Italian degree classes: it was created by Ministerial Decree (MUR) no. 146 of 09/02/2021, and Italian universities began enrolling into it from a.y. 2022/23; before it existed, data-science masters were normally placed in LM-91 or LM-82. unibz was using the LM-Data label for this programme at least as early as 2023 — its course-contents document is published as 'course-contents-LM-Data-2023.pdf' with the header 'MASTER IN DATA ANALYTICS FOR ECONOMICS AND MANAGEMENT (LM-Data)'. TWO DOCUMENT DEFECTS TO KNOW ABOUT, both harmless boilerplate but confusing if read literally: (1) the programme page and the admission-information PDF illustrate the dual-enrolment rule with 'e.g., LM-63/LM-63', which is the class of the Public Policy master, not of this programme; (2) both signed ranking-list decrees illustrate the same rule with 'e.g., LM-18/LM-18', which is the class of the Computing for Data Science master. Neither changes this programme's actual class, which is LM-Data throughout the official 'At a glance' data.
offered_in_2026_27: YES — running, and demonstrably so. Three pieces of hard evidence: (1) the 2026/27 admission-information PDF (footer 'Latest update: 24.08.2026') publishes the full 2026/27 calendar, including classes starting 28/09/2026; (2) both 2026/27 ranking lists have already been published as digitally signed decrees and the places were actually filled — 29 EU applicants admitted in the Early Bird session and 20 in the Late session, plus 10 non-EU admitted with a 30-name waiting list behind them; (3) the Additional Application Session page lists 'Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management (Application possible)' — twice, once under Economics and Management and once under Engineering. As of the verification date 2026-08-29 that additional window is STILL OPEN: applications run 18/08/2026 to 04/09/2026 by noon, so roughly six days remained at verification time. The additional session is restricted to EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment; non-EU applicants living abroad had only the single Early Bird window, which closed on 28/04/2026. Contrast with unibz programmes that appear on the site but are not recruiting (Professional Bachelor in Wood Technology, Master in Tourism Management) and with two Economics programmes for which the additional session was explicitly 'Application NOT offered' this year (Bachelor in Economics and Management, Master in Accounting and Finance).
is_new_programme: NOT a new programme in 2026/27, but it is a RECENT one and it is being substantially re-engineered this year, which is why it can read as new. Evidence on age: the earliest Internet Archive capture of the programme page is 30/01/2023; unibz's course-contents document for the programme is dated 2023 ('course-contents-LM-Data-2023.pdf'); a unibz LinkedIn post promoting the programme dates from February 2023; and course-offering pages exist for 2023, 2024 and 2025. The best reading of that evidence is a first intake in a.y. 2023/24, which would make 2026/27 roughly the fourth cohort — this inference is flagged as uncertain because unibz nowhere states an inaugural year and the Wayback archive could not be fetched directly for confirmation. Evidence of restructuring: the site navigation splits the curriculum into 'Course Offering - Enrolled from 2025' and 'Course Offering - Enrolled before 2025', so the study plan was revised for the 2025/26 cohort; and the genuinely new element for 2026/27 is the teaching model, not the degree — 'Starting from the academic year 2026/27, most courses in the Master will be delivered using the EDUNEXT model, an innovative teaching approach promoted by the Italian Universities Digital Hub.' The programme is 'co-funded by PNRR project EDUNEXT' (Italy's National Recovery and Resilience Plan). EDUNEXT means short high-quality online materials studied in advance, with classroom time reallocated to problem-solving, discussion and applied work on real-world datasets, under a problem-based learning approach. Practical implication for an applicant: expect a flipped-classroom, partly-online delivery in 2026/27 that earlier cohorts did not experience; unibz does not describe the programme as distance learning, and attendance in Bozen-Bolzano remains the model.
majors_tracks_study_plans: TWO TRACKS, chosen within one degree and one ranking list — there is no separate application per track, and the admission criteria, places and deadlines are identical for both. 'The programme is divided into two tracks: Data Analytics for Economics and Business Analytics. Both tracks share a strong methodological core in computer science, statistics, mathematics, and econometrics.' TRACK 1 — DATA ANALYTICS FOR ECONOMICS. Year 1 (60 CP): Programming and Visualisation for Data Science 12 CP (M1 Programming in Python 6 + M2 Data Analysis and Visualisation 6); Econometrics for Data Science 12 CP (M1 Management of Economic and Business Data 6 + M2 Time Series Analysis and Forecasting 6); Statistical Methods 12 CP (M1 Statistical Inference 6 + M2 Statistical and Machine Learning Methods for Business Analysis 6); Cybersecurity and Digital Privacy 3 CP; Responsible Data Practices for Business and Economics 3 CP; AI Methods for Decision Making 6 CP; Free choice course 6 CP; Impact Evaluation 6 CP. Year 2 (60 CP): Optimisation Methods for Decision Making 12 CP (M1 Optimisation Methods 6 + M2 Statistical Modeling for Sustainability and Risk Evaluation 6); Big Data Methods for Economics and Business 12 CP (M1 Language Processing and Web Analytics 6 + M2 Statistical Methods for High-Dimensional Data 6); Free choice course 6 CP; Financial Econometrics 6 CP; Analysis of Spatio-Temporal Data for Economics 6 CP; Internship 6 CP; Thesis 12 CP. TRACK 2 — BUSINESS ANALYTICS. Identical core; the three differentiating courses are Applied Data Science for Business Decision-Making 6 CP (year 1, in place of Impact Evaluation), and in year 2 Digital Marketing Methods and Consumer Experience 6 CP and Network Analysis for Business and Social Sciences 6 CP (in place of Financial Econometrics and Analysis of Spatio-Temporal Data for Economics); year 2 closes with Internship 6 CP and 'Final exam' 12 CP. Free choice: 12 CP in total across the two years; the Faculty Secretariat emails the eligible course list and the selection deadline each semester and the choice is submitted through the my SNS portal. PART-TIME VARIANT: 'Part-time enrolment allows you to reduce your study load... Students choose this option after enrollment (in October) and not during the application' — so it is not an application-stage decision and does not affect admission. Hands-on components advertised: building datasets in a flipped classroom and the Data4Econ Hackathon (team work, e.g. developing predictive models to forecast wind energy production).
english_only_accessibility: OPEN — genuinely and fully accessible to a candidate who speaks only English, and one of the cleanest cases in the whole unibz catalogue. Reasons: (1) the sole entry language requirement is English B2, and B2 is a comparatively low bar (IELTS 5.5-6.5, TOEFL iBT 72-94); (2) no Italian or German is required to be admitted, to study, to sit exams, or — as far as any published document shows — to graduate; (3) no interview, no entrance test, no portfolio and no motivation letter, so there is no oral stage in which another language could surface; (4) the entire selection is document-based and the documents may be submitted in Italian, German OR English; (5) an English-medium bachelor is itself recognised as C1, which simultaneously satisfies the entry requirement and earns the 5-point language bonus. Two practical caveats that are about administration, not language of study: everyday life and public administration in Bozen-Bolzano operate in German and Italian, and the third-language B1 rule that unibz applies to its trilingual programmes (B1 needed to sit curricular exams in that language) has no counterpart here because there is no third language in this study plan. For a Turkish applicant with an English-taught bachelor, this programme is effectively as open as it gets: the whole procedure can be completed in English end to end.
admission_type: RESTRICTED ACCESS (numero programmato) with a purely document-based, points-scored ranking list — no examination of any kind. Concretely: (a) no entrance exam, no TOLC, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GMAT/GRE; (b) no interview; (c) no portfolio, video, project proposal or motivation letter; (d) no admission test on subject knowledge. What decides your place is arithmetic on your transcript: your grade average converted to a 0-88 scale, plus up to 12 points of bonuses, against a minimum of 55 points and against the other applicants in the same session. Language proficiency functions as an eligibility gate, not as a scored test: fail to evidence English B2 by the application deadline and 'you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. Everything is submitted through the online Application Portal (https://aws.unibz.it/exup). An Admission Committee then evaluates and signs a ranking-list decree. Committee for 2026/27 (identical in both sessions): President Prof. F. Marta L. Di Lascio; members Prof. Alessandro Casa and Prof. Davide Ferrari. Appeals against the ranking list may be lodged with the Bozen-Bolzano Administrative Court within 60 days of notification or publication.
academic_requirements: A THREE-YEAR UNIVERSITY DEGREE PLUS 24 ECTS IN SPECIFIED SUBJECT AREAS. Verbatim: 'a three-year university degree (*) in one of the degree classes pursuant to Italian Ministerial Decree No. 270/04 (or an equivalent Italian qualification from previous degree programmes as well as an equivalent qualification gained abroad and recognised as suitable) and the attainment of the following university credit points (ECTS) in the following subject areas'. (*) footnote: 'Italian citizen who have obtained their degree abroad must also have a secondary school leaving qualification.' At enrolment a foreign degree must be evidenced by a Diploma Supplement showing at least 180 ECTS and that the qualification gives access to a master programme. BLOCK A — at least 12 ECTS in 'Economics' or 'Business Administration', in these Italian scientific-disciplinary sectors (2024-reform code first, pre-reform code in brackets): ECON-01/A Economics (ex SECS-P/01); ECON-02/A Economic policy (ex SECS-P/02); ECON-03/A Public Economics (ex SECS-P/03); ECON-05/A Econometrics (ex SECS-P/05); ECON-04/A Applied economics (ex SECS-P/06); ECON-06/A Business administration and accounting studies (ex SECS-P/07); ECON-07/A Management (ex SECS-P/08); ECON-09/A Corporate finance (ex SECS-P/09); ECON-08/A Organization and human resource management (ex SECS-P/10); ECON-09/B Financial markets and institutions (ex SECS-P/11); IEGE-01/A Business and management engineering (ex ING-IND/35). BLOCK B — 'At least 12 ECTS in "Statistics-Mathematics" and/or "Computer Science", of which at least 2 ECTS must be in the "Computer Science" field', in these sectors: STAT-01/A Statistics (ex SECS-S/01); STAT-01/B Statistics for Experimental and Technological Research (ex SECS-S/02); STAT-02/A Economic Statistics (ex SECS-S/03); STAT-03/A Demography (ex SECS-S/04); STAT-03/B Social Statistics (ex SECS-S/05); STAT-04/A Mathematical methods of economics, finance and actuarial science (ex SECS-S/06); MATH-02/A Algebra (ex MAT/02); MATH-02/B Geometry (ex MAT/03); MATH-03/A Mathematical Analysis (ex MAT/05); MATH-03/B Probability and Statistics (ex MAT/06); MATH-06/A Operations research (ex MAT/09); INFO-01/A Computer Science (ex INF/01); IINF-05/A Information processing system (ex ING-INF/05). READING THIS AS A FOREIGN APPLICANT: SSD codes exist only on Italian transcripts, so for a Turkish or other foreign bachelor the Faculty maps your courses onto these areas from the transcript and, where it needs to, from syllabi — 'The Faculty reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary.' The mandatory Excel study-career template is precisely the instrument used to make that mapping. The embedded 2-ECTS computer-science minimum inside Block B is the trap most non-Italian applicants miss: a pure economics or pure statistics bachelor with no programming/informatics course can satisfy 12+12 in aggregate and still fail. TWO ANTI-DOUBLE-COUNTING RULES: 'Courses included in the programme of the Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management are not valid for the acquisition of the 24 CPs required for admission' (so you cannot pre-take this master's own courses as a single-subject student to qualify), and 'Courses that have been taken into consideration in order to achieve the 24 CPs necessary to gain admission to the master programme cannot be recognised for a possible career abbreviation' (credits spent on eligibility cannot later be reused to shorten the degree). Dual enrolment: 'simultaneous enrolment in a maximum of 2 programmes is possible (however, the two programmes must not belong to the same class... and must differ for at least 2/3 of the course contents).'
entry_exam_or_test: NONE. There is no entrance examination for this programme in any form — no unibz subject test, no TOLC-E/TOLC-I, no CENT-S, no SAT, no GMAT or GRE (neither required nor rewarded), no mathematics admission test and therefore no OFA mechanism. The admission-information PDF's 'Admission procedure' section lists exactly three scored criteria (grade average, further language proficiency, academic background) and no test. The only examination that can appear anywhere in this process is OPTIONAL and purely linguistic: the unibz Language Centre's computer-based English proficiency exam, which exists solely as a fourth way of evidencing B2 for applicants who cannot document it otherwise. Its 2026/27 sittings were: Early Bird — 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026; this date was marked FULLY BOOKED on the Language Centre page) and 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026, with 21/04 as a technical make-up day); Late — 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026, with 26/06 as make-up day). A further date of 27/07/2026 (registration 10-19/07/2026) was offered only to applicants to inter-university programmes. NO language exams are offered for the Additional Application Session at all — applicants in that window must arrive with a certificate already in hand, and unibz specifically recommends LanguageCert, TOEFL or IELTS 'as the results of these exams are generally available within a short period of time'. Rule when sitting the exam: 'It is not possible to take exams at different levels for the same language.' Compensatory measures (extra time, assistive IT) are available to candidates with disabilities who notify Student Support by the exam registration deadline.
selection_scoring: MAXIMUM 100 POINTS, MINIMUM 55 TO ENTER THE RANKING. The rubric, verbatim from the admission-information PDF and both signed ranking-list decrees: '1. Grade average (max. 88 points) + "cum laude" (2 points) — If you have already graduated: Final grade (expressed in thirtieths). If you have not graduated yet: The grade average of the passed university exams (expressed in thirtieths). In case of a bachelor concluded with the highest grade and the mention "summa cum laude", 2 additional points will be awarded. 2. Further language proficiency: You will receive 5 points if you demonstrate at least a C1 level in the official language of instruction (English). 3. Academic background: You will receive 5 points if you have earned more than 24 credit points (ECTS/CFUs) in the scientific-disciplinary sectors required for admission to the programme. Minimum total points required to be admitted to the ranking: 55 points.' So the arithmetic is 88 + 2 + 5 + 5 = 100, and the grade average carries 88-90% of the weight — this is overwhelmingly a GPA-driven selection in which the two 5-point bonuses act as tie-breakers between similar transcripts. TIE-BREAK RULE: 'According to Art. 26, Paragraph 2), letter b) of the current admission regulation, in the event of equal scores, priority will be given to the applicant who has obtained a higher partial score for the more heavily weighted evaluation criterion for determining the overall score of the ranking list. If scores are still equal, the younger applicant will have priority.' COMPLETENESS RULE: 'Only complete applications will be considered. The absence of one or more of the documents required for the calculation of the average marks will result in exclusion.' WHAT THE SCORE ACTUALLY HAD TO BE IN 2026/27 (from the signed decrees — far more informative than the 55-point floor): EU/parity Early Bird — 29 admitted, top score 100.00, lowest admitted 73.10; EU/parity Late — 20 admitted, top 97.20, lowest admitted 70.43; non-EU living abroad Early Bird — 10 admitted, top 94.38, lowest admitted 88.03, with a waiting list running from 87.02 down to 62.45 at rank 40. Read that carefully: the real competitive threshold for a non-EU applicant was about 88 points, some 33 points above the formal minimum and roughly 15 points above the EU cut-off, because 40 qualified non-EU applicants were competing for 10 places. A DOCUMENT DEFECT worth knowing: the Early Bird decree prints criterion 1 as 'Grade average (max. 90 88 points)' — an uncorrected edit artefact where 90 was replaced by 88; the Late decree and the admission-information PDF both print the clean '88 points', so 88 is the operative figure.
bonus_points: THREE BONUSES, 12 POINTS MAXIMUM, all mechanical and all documented in the same rubric. (1) 'cum laude' — 2 points, awarded only 'In case of a bachelor concluded with the highest grade and the mention "summa cum laude"'; for a foreign degree this means the top-of-scale distinction, and it therefore requires that your transcript state the grading scale (minimum passing and maximum achievable final grade), which unibz demands anyway for foreign qualifications. (2) English at C1 or above — 5 points, over and above the B2 needed to be eligible at all. This is the single easiest bonus for an international applicant to capture, because unibz recognises an English-medium secondary-school final year OR an English-medium bachelor/master degree as C1 automatically, with no test; failing that, IELTS 7.0-8.0, TOEFL iBT 95-113, C1 Advanced (CAE) grade B or C, PTE Academic 76-84 or telc English C1 all qualify. (3) Academic background — 5 points 'if you have earned more than 24 credit points (ECTS/CFUs) in the scientific-disciplinary sectors required for admission'. Note the wording: MORE than 24, i.e. strictly above the 12+12 eligibility floor, so an applicant with a quantitatively heavy bachelor gets this almost automatically while a minimally-qualifying applicant does not. WHAT IS NOT AWARDED HERE (relevant because sister unibz programmes do award these): there is NO Webometrics university-ranking bonus (Computing for Data Science and Software Engineering give 1-3 points for the applicant's home university's world rank; this programme gives none), NO GMAT/GRE bonus (Accounting and Finance offers one), NO start-up or project-presentation points (Entrepreneurship and Innovation offers 30), and no points for work experience, internships, publications or motivation. In practice, an applicant who holds an English-taught quantitative bachelor should expect to bank 10 of the 12 bonus points, which is why the effective competition sits in the high 80s and 90s.
portfolio_and_materials: NONE REQUIRED — and this is a genuine simplification relative to most unibz masters. No portfolio, no video, no research or project proposal, no motivation letter, no letters of recommendation, no CV and no writing sample appear anywhere in the admission-information PDF, the brochure, the programme page or the two signed ranking-list decrees. There are consequently no format limits to observe (nothing equivalent to the Design faculty's 20 MB portfolio PDF, the 2-A4 project proposal, the 6,000-character motivation letter or the 2-minute video used elsewhere at unibz). The complete upload set is transcript-and-identity evidence plus one structured spreadsheet — see 'required_documents'. The only content you author yourself is the Excel study-career template, and that is data entry, not persuasive writing, which also means there is no place in this application where an applicant can compensate for a weaker grade average with a strong narrative.
interview: NO INTERVIEW. No interview, oral examination, online meeting or motivational conversation is part of this admission procedure at any stage, for either EU or non-EU applicants, in any of the three sessions. Neither the admission-information PDF nor either signed ranking-list decree mentions one, and neither publishes interview dates. This differs from sister unibz programmes that do interview — for example the Master in Computing for Data Science interviews applicants who fall below its scoring threshold (dates 22 and 26 May 2026). Here there is no below-threshold rescue route of any kind: an application scoring under 55 points, or missing a document needed to compute the average, is simply excluded, with notification by e-mail and — for Early Bird applicants only — the option to reapply in a later session ('Excluded applicants will be notified by e-mail and can apply again in the 2nd session'). The Admission Committee (Di Lascio, Casa, Ferrari) evaluates 'only the documents uploaded in the portal by the application deadline'.
conditional_admission: YES — 140 ECTS, not the 120 used by most unibz masters, and this is the single most important procedural detail for a final-year bachelor student. Verbatim: 'If you have not yet graduated at the time of application: You can apply if you have acquired at least 140 credit points (ECTS). In this case you will be admitted conditionally, and you will need to submit your diploma by the enrolment deadline.' IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO A COMMON ASSUMPTION: 140 is NOT unique to this programme and is not an extra hurdle invented for it — it is the Faculty of Economics and Management's standard threshold, shared with the Master in Accounting and Finance, the Master in Entrepreneurship and Innovation and the Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance. It is higher than the 120 ECTS used by the Engineering-side masters (Computing for Data Science, Software Engineering, Smart Technologies for Sports and Health) and by EMMA, and higher than Industrial Mechanical Engineering's 135. Practical effect: with 140 of 180 ECTS required, you must be within roughly 40 ECTS of finishing — realistically in the final semester — at the moment you apply, and the Early Bird window closes on 28/04/2026, so a Turkish student on a normal June/July graduation cycle needs to have banked those 140 credits by late April. HOW THE SCORE IS COMPUTED IF YOU HAVE NOT GRADUATED: your ranking score uses 'The grade average of the passed university exams (expressed in thirtieths)', not a final degree grade, and you appear in the list with an asterisk as provisionally admitted. This is heavily used in practice: 13 of the 29 EU Early Bird admits, 9 of the 20 EU Late admits and 1 of the 10 non-EU admits were asterisked as not yet holding the bachelor. THE HARD DEADLINE AND THE MONEY TRAP: 'requirement for admission is the conclusion of the bachelor studies by the enrolment deadline (13 October 2026, 12 midday)'. Miss it and 'You cannot enrol and you will lose your place, which will be offered to the subsequent applicant in the ranking list.' unibz gives explicit financial advice about this: 'In this case you should not pay the tuition fees to secure your admission' — because the first instalment is non-refundable for EU applicants. The consolation route: 'You will be able to submit a late enrolment request and, only if there still are available places, you will be allowed to enrol by 11 December 2026' (the decrees add that this request goes to the Rector). A SEPARATE RESERVATION applies to foreign qualifications regardless of graduation status: 'Applicants with qualifications gained abroad who have not uploaded their diploma are provisionally admitted until their study title can be verified', and for non-EU applicants living abroad, ALL admissions are provisional pending the consulate's official communication to unibz. Finally, the reservation can bite even after you are enrolled: 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.'
ofa_rules: NOT APPLICABLE. OFA (obblighi formativi aggiuntivi / additional learning requirements) is an Italian first-cycle instrument: it is assigned to bachelor students who fail a compulsory entry test, and at unibz it applies to open-access bachelors such as Economics and Management, Economics Politics and Ethics, and Tourism Sport and Event Management, whose applicants sit a compulsory mathematics test. This is a second-cycle, restricted-access programme with no entry test at all, so no OFA can be assigned. The functional equivalent at master level — the mechanism that ensures incoming students have the prerequisite background — is handled entirely up front and as a pass/fail eligibility gate, not as a remediable debt: you must already hold 12 ECTS in economics/business and 12 ECTS in statistics-mathematics/computer science (with at least 2 in computer science) at the moment of application. If you do not, you are excluded; there is no provision to enrol first and make up the shortfall later, and unibz explicitly forbids using this master's own courses to acquire the missing 24 CP. Optional (non-remedial) preparatory offerings exist for all incoming students: intensive language courses 01-18/09/2026 and optional pre-courses 21/09-09/10/2026.
language_requirements: ENGLISH B2 TO BE ADMITTED — one language, one level, no exceptions, and it is an exclusion gate rather than a scored item. Verbatim: 'The official teaching language is English. Therefore, the following language requirements apply, otherwise you will be excluded from the admission procedure: Entry level (to gain admission) English: B2. The levels of the Common European Framework of Reference apply.' No Italian and no German is required at any level, on entry or during the programme. Demonstrating C1 instead of B2 is optional and is rewarded with 5 ranking points. The proof must be in place BY THE APPLICATION DEADLINE of the session you are applying in — 'The language proficiency requirements for admission must be met by the stated pre-registration deadline' — not by enrolment, and not by the start of classes; this is the most common way otherwise-qualified international applicants lose a place. Evidence is uploaded in the Application Portal under 'upload language certificates' and/or 'enrol for language exams', which only become available after you have created an application under 'create/manage applications'. Formal difference by issuer: 'In case your final certificate has been awarded by an Italian public institution, you need to submit a self-declaration. In case your final certificate has been awarded by a foreign public institution, you need to upload diploma scanned copy of the original.' Certificates that cannot be uploaded may be e-mailed as PDF or delivered in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline.
entry_levels_by_position: 1st language English B2; NO second language; NO third language. unibz's position-based system (levels attach to the 1st/2nd/3rd language slot rather than to a named language) exists for its trilingual programmes and is effectively degenerate here, because this master has exactly one language of instruction. Written in the comparative form unibz uses elsewhere, this programme is 'B2 / none / none'. Compare, within the same university and the same admission cycle: Master in Public Policy and Innovative Governance C1/B2/none (trilingual, and effectively closed to an English-only applicant); Bachelor in Computer Science B2/B2/none; Bachelor in Electronic and Information Engineering B2/B1/none; Master in Accounting and Finance C1/B2/none. Against that field, a single B2 in English is the lowest and simplest language barrier unibz applies to any of its degree programmes, and it is the reason this master is one of the few genuinely open to a monolingual English speaker. There is no language-position declaration to make in the application, and no rule here about which language counts as your first — the concept does not apply.
exit_levels: NO EXIT (GRADUATION) LANGUAGE REQUIREMENT IS PUBLISHED FOR THIS PROGRAMME. This is a documented absence rather than a stated rule, so treat it as high-confidence but not quotable: the admission-information PDF contains an 'Entry level (to gain admission)' heading with nothing beside it, and no 'Exit level (to graduate)' section at all — whereas the corresponding documents for unibz's trilingual programmes do carry an explicit 'Exit level (to graduate)' block (typically 1st language C1, 2nd language C1, 3rd language B1). The programme page reproduces the same structure, with an entry level and no exit level. The Faculty of Economics and Management's Study Guide pages on the master final exam and on study plans likewise set out thesis and free-choice-credit rules with no language condition attached to graduation. The logical reading is that the trilingual exit-level regime exists to enforce plurilingualism in trilingual degrees and has no object in a mono-lingual English degree: the student is already studying and examined in English throughout, and the 12 CP thesis/final exam is in English. Recommended action for an applicant who needs certainty: confirm with the Faculty Secretariat (schoolofeconomics@unibz.it, +39 0471 013000) or the Language Centre before enrolling, since a negative finding derived from silence in the sources is exactly the kind of item unibz could clarify differently in a study regulation published only in Italian or German. Flagged as uncertain for that reason.
third_language_exam_threshold: NOT APPLICABLE — there is no third language in this programme. The unibz rule that a B1 level in the third language is 'the minimum requirement for taking curricular exams in the respective language' (restated on the Additional Application Session page, which advises third-language beginners to reach A1 before classes start and describes the standard Language Centre path from A1 to B1 running October 2026 to September 2027) governs trilingual degrees where some examinations are actually held in Italian or German. In this master every course, every examination and the final thesis are in English, so no B1-in-a-third-language gate can arise and none is mentioned in the programme's own documents. Practical corollary: an admitted student here is never blocked from sitting an exam for linguistic reasons, and the September intensive language courses (01-18/09/2026) and A1 courses from mid-October are optional enrichment rather than obligations — though a student intending to work locally in South Tyrol afterwards would find German and Italian valuable for the labour market rather than for the degree. Flagged as uncertain only in the weak sense that it rests on the absence of any contrary provision.
proof_pathways: FOUR ACCEPTED WAYS TO EVIDENCE ENGLISH, exactly as enumerated in the admission-information PDF. (1) SECONDARY SCHOOL — 'the main teaching language in your final high school year, if English (recognised as C1)'. Note this yields C1, so it satisfies B2 eligibility AND earns the 5-point bonus in one step. 'Foreign qualifications: If the main teaching language is not clearly stated on your high school diploma, please also upload a letter/document issued by your high school stating the medium of instruction' — for Turkish and other non-EU applicants this supporting letter is usually indispensable, because national diplomas rarely name the medium of instruction. (2) PRIOR DEGREE — 'a bachelor or master degree in English (recognised as C1)', again worth the bonus; 'unibz graduates must upload the language certificates obtained and/or declare that they have passed language exams at the unibz Language Centre (B2, B2+ or C1)'; and for foreign degrees, 'If the teaching language is not clearly stated on your University degree, please also upload a letter/document issued by your University stating the medium of instruction during your studies.' (3) RECOGNISED CERTIFICATE — from the official list (see certificate_rules); uploadable in the portal, or 'If you cannot upload the certificates, you can send them by e-mail as PDF files or deliver them in person to the Language Centre by the application deadline'. (4) UNIBZ LANGUAGE CENTRE EXAM — registered online through the portal under 'enrol for language exams' after the application has been filled in; note the warning that 'If you start your application outside a language exams registration period, you must return to the portal during one of the periods indicated above in order to register for an exam'. 2026/27 EXAM AND REGISTRATION WINDOWS: Early Bird — exam 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026; shown as FULLY BOOKED, spots limited) and exams 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026; 21/04 is a make-up day for technical issues); Late — exams 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026; 26/06 make-up day); plus 27/07/2026 (registration 10-19/07/2026) reserved for inter-university programme applicants. All 2026/27 sittings were held ONLINE. The system auto-detects which modules you must take (full exam or retakes of modules II and/or III), which determines whether you sit in the morning, the afternoon or both. CRITICAL GAP: no Language Centre exams are offered for the Additional Application Session — an applicant in the 18/08-04/09/2026 window must already hold acceptable evidence, and unibz recommends LanguageCert, TOEFL or IELTS for speed, noting which of these are accepted in 'Home Edition' format.
certificate_rules: GOVERNED BY RESOLUTION OF THE UNIVERSITY COUNCIL No. 16/2026 ('Recognised language certificates and diplomas - Students and applicants'), published trilingually at /assets/Documents/Languages/unibz-recognised-language-certificates-v2.pdf. GENERAL RULES, verbatim: a certificate must 'include the assessment in all four skills and the certificate must be issued by the certification organisation itself' and 'indicate adequate performance in all skills in the form of an overall grade'; 'If no overall result and/or level is stated on the certificate, the lowest level reached in one of the subskills is decisive for determining the level'; 'There is no compensation for "failed" parts of the exam and no averages are calculated unless these provided by the certification organisation'; 'Certificates issued by exam boards and obtained by taking an online exam ("home edition") are not recognised, except for those explicitly indicated in the list'; 'Certificates regarding single skills issued by different certification organisations will not be accepted'; 'Certificates of participation, certificates of end-of-course-tests and examinations from private educational institutions as well as results of placement tests will not be recognised'; 'Certificates issued by individual lecturers or teaching staff will not be recognised. DAAD certificates are not recognised.' VALIDITY: 'International language certificates must not be older than five years before the date of their submission. The entire calendar year shall apply from 1 January' — i.e. certificates issued from 1 January of the fifth year preceding submission remain valid for the whole of that year. Items in the 'Further Recognised Degrees, Diplomas and Certificates' section (English-medium schooling, English-medium degrees, unibz internal exams) have UNLIMITED validity — a decisive advantage for applicants with an English-taught bachelor, whose evidence never expires. ENGLISH CERTIFICATES AND THE B2/C1 BOUNDARIES THAT MATTER HERE (B2 = eligible; C1 = eligible + 5 bonus points): IELTS Academic or General 5.5-6.5 = B2, 7.0-8.0 = C1, 8.5+ = C2 (home edition accepted). TOEFL iBT 72-94 = B2, 95-113 = C1, 114-120 = C2 (home edition accepted). Cambridge: B2 First grade B or C = B2, B2 First grade A = C1, C1 Advanced grade B or C = C1, C1 Advanced grade A = C2, and note C1 Advanced taken but scored at level B2 counts only as B2. PTE Academic 59-75 = B2, 76-84 = C1. Pearson PEIC B2/C1; LanguageCert General/Academic/ESOL B2 and C1 (Academic variants home-edition accepted); Trinity ISE II = B2, ISE III = C1; telc English B2/C1; Michigan MET B2/C1 (all four skills) and ECCE = B2, ECPE = C2; TOEIC Listening 400+/Reading 385+/Speaking 160+/Writing 150+ = B2 and Listening 490+/Reading 455+/Speaking 180+/Writing 180+ = C1 (home edition accepted); Gatehouse Classic IESOL and GATE B2/C1; English Speaking Board Level 1 = B2, Level 2 = C1; Oxford Test of English B2 (no C1 listed); Aptis ESOL General/Advanced B2 and C1; UNIcert Level II = B2, Level III = C1; IGCSE/GCSE English as a second language grade A/B/C = B2, and 'IGCSE and GCSE qualifications containing A levels are considered secondary school diplomas with English as predominant language of instruction'. UNLIMITED-VALIDITY ENGLISH EVIDENCE: unibz Language Centre internal B2 and C1 exams; bi- and multilingual international secondary schools with English as one of the languages of instruction = B2; secondary school with English as predominant language of instruction = C1; diploma with explicit annotation of the level reached. PRACTICAL WARNINGS for a Turkish applicant: Duolingo English Test does NOT appear on the list; a YDS/e-YDS or YÖKDİL result does not appear either; the four-skills requirement rules out certificates lacking a speaking or writing component; and because the lowest sub-skill sets the level, an IELTS 7.0 overall with a 6.0 in writing is treated as B2, not C1, and forfeits the 5-point bonus.
application_deadline_eu: THREE SEPARATE SESSIONS for EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment, all closing at 12:00 noon local (Italian) time. Normalised to ISO from unibz's DD/MM/YYYY: (1) EARLY BIRD — opens 2026-03-02, closes 2026-04-28 12:00. This is the main and largest session (30 of the 40 EU places) and the ONLY session open to non-EU applicants living abroad, so it is the one an international applicant must plan around. (2) LATE APPLICATION (EU only) — opens 2026-05-28, closes 2026-07-08 12:00. (3) ADDITIONAL APPLICATION SESSION (EU only) — opens 2026-08-18, closes 2026-09-04 12:00; this session exists at the Faculty's discretion, 'The Faculty can open additional application sessions for single study programmes in August and in September if there are available places', and for 2026/27 the Additional Application Session page confirms 'Master in Data Analytics for Economics and Management (Application possible)'. As of the verification date 2026-08-29 the additional window was still open with about six days left. Two rules that affect strategy: an applicant excluded in the first session may reapply in the second ('If you are excluded in the first session, you might apply again in the second one'), and applicants may apply to more than one study programme. Each session has its own language-exam registration window (see proof_pathways) except the additional session, which offers none. Applications go through the online portal at https://aws.unibz.it/exup; 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified. Filled-in forms which have not been sent correctly will not be taken into consideration.'
application_deadline_non_eu: ONE WINDOW ONLY: 2026-03-02 to 2026-04-28, 12:00 noon local time (the Early Bird session). This applies to non-EU citizens living outside Italy, which is the relevant category for most Turkish applicants. Verbatim: 'Only one application period is offered. After the deadline it is not possible to apply anymore.' There is no late session and no additional session for this group — both the Late Application and the Additional Application Session are explicitly EU-only — so a missed Early Bird deadline means waiting a full year. Ten places are contested in that single window; in 2026/27 forty applicants qualified for them, and the tenth-ranked admit scored 88.03. A non-refundable application fee of €50 applies to this category only. The downstream chain is equally rigid: ranking list by 2026-05-27, first instalment by 2026-06-05 12:00, then the mandatory Universitaly pre-enrolment and visa application, then enrolment by 2026-10-13 12:00. A non-EU applicant who holds a valid Italian residence permit for work, family, political or humanitarian asylum, or religious reasons is NOT in this category — see parity_of_treatment — and would instead use the EU sessions and pay no application fee.
parity_of_treatment: THREE CATEGORIES, and the third is the one that changes a Turkish applicant's entire timetable. Verbatim: 'Considered as equivalent are: 1. Citizens from Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Switzerland, San Marino and the Vatican City State; 2. Non-EU citizens with a valid permit to stay in Italy (see article 39, paragraph 5 of decree no. 286 of 25.07.1998: "permesso di soggiorno" (residence permit) for work, family reasons, political or humanitarian asylum, religious reasons). In this case, you apply directly to the University as described above and must submit a copy of your valid permit to stay. A permit to stay for study reasons or a visa for tourism is not valid. If the permit has expired, you must attach a renewal request.' THE PENALTY FOR NOT UPLOADING IT: 'Please note that if you do not upload the permit in the application portal, you will be automatically considered a non-EU citizen living abroad and therefore subject to the admission procedure through the Italian authorities in your country of origin.' WHY THIS MATTERS SO MUCH HERE: the difference is not cosmetic. A Turkish citizen already resident in Italy on a work or family permit competes for 40 EU places across three sessions running from March to early September, pays no €50 fee, needs no Universitaly pre-enrolment and no student visa — and in 2026/27 would have needed only 73.10 points in the Early Bird session or 70.43 in the Late session. The same person applying from Turkey competes for 10 places in a single spring window and would have needed 88.03. The excluded cases are equally important: a study permit does not count (so an exchange or language student in Italy stays in the non-EU-abroad category), and neither does a tourist visa. A permit under renewal is acceptable if the renewal request is attached. Both signed ranking-list decrees keep the two populations in physically separate lists headed 'EU CITIZENS AND CITIZEN ENJOYING PARITY OF TREATMENT' and 'NON-EU CITIZENS LIVING ABROAD', with no crossover between them.
places_quotas: 50 PLACES IN TOTAL, split into three quotas that never cross. From the admission-information PDF: 'Available places — EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment: Early Bird Application: 30; Late Application: 10. Non-EU citizens (living abroad): Early Bird Application: 10.' The 'At a glance' box aggregates this as 'Places available: 40 EU + 10 non-EU'. ROLL-OVER RULE: 'For EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment only: any remaining places of the early bird application, will be offered in the late application' — so the Late quota is a floor, not a ceiling. That rule is visible in the 2026/27 outcome: 29 EU applicants were admitted in Early Bird (one place short of the 30) yet 20 were admitted in the Late session against a nominal 10, which is consistent with early-bird places freed by admitted applicants who never confirmed being pushed into the second session (this reading is an inference from the two decrees, not an explicit unibz statement). WHAT THE COMPETITION LOOKED LIKE IN 2026/27: EU/parity Early Bird — 29 admitted, scores 100.00 down to 73.10, of whom 13 provisionally admitted pending completion of the bachelor; EU/parity Late — 20 admitted, scores 97.20 down to 70.43, of whom 9 provisional; non-EU living abroad — 10 admitted filling all 10 places, scores 94.38 down to 88.03, plus a waiting list of 30 further applicants from rank 11 (87.02) to rank 40 (62.45), to be contacted by e-mail as of 8 June 2026 if a place opened. The structural asymmetry is the headline: the non-EU quota is 20% of the total, was 4x oversubscribed among qualified applicants alone, and demanded a score roughly 15 points higher than the EU cut-off. The additional session for 2026/27 adds an unspecified further number of EU places (it is opened only 'if there are available places'), and its ranking list was due by 18/09/2026 — after the verification date.
ranking_and_enrolment_dates: THREE PARALLEL CHAINS, one per session, each with the same three-step structure: ranking list published, first instalment paid to lock the place, then enrolment. All times are 12:00 noon local (Italian) time; ISO conversions in brackets. EARLY BIRD (EU and non-EU) — publication of ranking lists by 27/05/2026 [2026-05-27]; payment of the 1st instalment of €600 by 05/06/2026 noon [2026-06-05]; enrolment from 10/07/2026 to 13/10/2026 noon [2026-07-10 to 2026-10-13]; non-EU waiting-list candidates contacted from 8 June 2026. LATE (EU only) — publication by 30/07/2026 [2026-07-30]; 1st instalment by 06/08/2026 noon [2026-08-06]; enrolment from publication of the ranking list until 13/10/2026 noon. ADDITIONAL SESSION (EU only) — publication by 18/09/2026 [2026-09-18]; 1st instalment by 25/09/2026 noon [2026-09-25]; enrolment from publication until 13/10/2026 noon. THE COMMON HARD STOP is 13/10/2026 noon: every session, whatever its start, funnels into that single enrolment deadline, which is also the date by which a conditionally admitted applicant must hold the bachelor diploma. LATE-ENROLMENT SAFETY NET: 11 December 2026, on request to the Rector and 'only if there are study places still available'. WHAT EACH STEP MEANS: missing the instalment deadline is automatic exclusion and the place passes to the next in line; paying does NOT make you a student — 'Paying university fees does not confer student status, which is only obtained by enrolling' — and unibz recommends enrolling as early as possible so that incomplete documents can be corrected before the deadline. Multiple offers: you may secure at most 2 programmes by paying the fee twice, and confirming a place means renouncing admission to the others. Non-refundability: no refund if you pay and do not enrol, the sole exception being non-EU applicants living abroad who fail to obtain the necessary documents from the Italian authorities in their country. Transfers from another Italian university require a copy of the transfer application to be filed with the Student Office at the start of the academic year. FOR CONTEXT, the academic year that follows: intensive language courses 01-18/09/2026; optional pre-courses 21/09-09/10/2026; Freshers Days 28-29/09/2026; 1st-semester classes 28/09-23/12/2026 and 07-23/01/2027, exams 25/01-20/02/2027 (extraordinary session 10-23/12/2026); 2nd-semester classes 01/03-25/03/2027 and 30/03-12/06/2027, exams 15/06-10/07/2027 (extraordinary session 12-22/05/2027); autumn exam session 23/08-25/09/2027.
programme_specific_dates: THERE ARE NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC ADMISSION EVENTS — no entrance-test date, no interview date, no portfolio submission date, no assessment-centre day. Everything on this programme's calendar is either a university-wide session date or a teaching date, which is unusual and simplifies planning considerably compared with, say, Design (portfolio) or Computing for Data Science (May interviews). The dates that do belong specifically to this programme's 2026/27 cycle are: application windows 02/03-28/04/2026, 28/05-08/07/2026 and 18/08-04/09/2026 (all closing at noon); ranking lists by 27/05, 30/07 and 18/09/2026; instalment deadlines 05/06, 06/08 and 25/09/2026 (noon); a single enrolment cut-off of 13/10/2026 noon with a Rector-approved late route to 11/12/2026; non-EU waiting-list contact from 08/06/2026. Language Centre exam dates attached to the sessions: 16/03/2026 (registration 02-09/03/2026, marked FULLY BOOKED), 16-17 and 20-21/04/2026 (registration 24/03-08/04/2026, 21/04 make-up), 22-26/06/2026 (registration 28/05-15/06/2026, 26/06 make-up), and 27/07/2026 (registration 10-19/07/2026) restricted to inter-university programme applicants; no exams at all for the additional session. Pre-teaching dates: intensive language courses 01-18/09/2026, optional pre-courses 21/09-09/10/2026, Freshers Days 28-29/09/2026, classes from 28/09/2026. The admission-information PDF's own currency stamp is 'Subject to change. Latest update: 24.08.2026', so all of the above reflect a document refreshed five days before the verification date. Recurring in-programme events with no fixed published date: the Data4Econ Hackathon and flipped-classroom dataset-building sessions; the internship of at least 150 hours is scheduled by the student across the two years.
required_documents: A SHORT, STRICTLY TRANSCRIPT-CENTRED LIST — five items, one of them a structured spreadsheet. (1) IDENTITY — an account in the Application Portal plus 'a valid ID card or passport (front/back)', with an explicit exclusion: 'if your document is invalid, incomplete or unreadable, you will be excluded from the admission procedure'. (2) QUALIFICATION — 'if graduated in Italy: diploma supplement or self-declaration (following the Italian D.P.R. no. 445/2000) of the degree awarded with the exams passed (if graduated) or with the exams passed (if not graduated yet); if graduated abroad: diploma supplement or final degree certificate with exams passed (if graduated) or transcript of records (if not graduated yet) in Italian, German or English.' The document 'must contain the following information: final grade, exams passed with grade and date of passing, credit points, scientific fields (the latter only for Italian titles). For qualifications obtained abroad, also: scale of grades awarded by the university of provenance (with a minimum final grade to obtain the qualification and a maximum final grade achievable).' That grading-scale requirement is mandatory, not optional, for a Turkish transcript — without it the 88-point conversion cannot be computed and 'The absence of one or more of the documents required for the calculation of the average marks will result in exclusion.' (3) THE EXCEL FILE — mandatory and structured: 'Please download the file available in the application portal. Fill in all information about your bachelor/courses and upload it in the portal as an excel file.' This is the study-career template through which the Faculty maps your courses onto the required subject areas and counts the 24 ECTS; it must be uploaded in Excel format, not as a PDF or scan. (4) DIPLOMA (foreign qualifications) — 'If you gained your qualification abroad, you must also upload the diploma of your qualification: if you are not yet in possession of the diploma, you'll need to upload it upon enrolment.' (5) LANGUAGE EVIDENCE — certificate upload or Language Centre exam registration, per proof_pathways; plus, for parity-of-treatment applicants, a copy of the valid permit to stay. AT ENROLMENT, additionally, for a foreign degree: the bachelor degree diploma; an official translation into Italian (not needed if issued in German or English); a Diploma Supplement stating at least 180 ECTS and that the qualification gives access to a master programme; and the ARDI/CIMEA statements described in credential_recognition. STANDING WARNINGS: 'Mendacious declarations will be criminally prosecuted and will result in the automatic exclusion from the ranking list'; 'Once the application has been sent, it cannot be modified'; and the Faculty 'reserves the right to request a description of the contents of the courses and/or teaching hours where necessary'.
application_fee: €50, charged ONLY to non-EU citizens living abroad, and non-refundable. Verbatim from the non-EU section of the admission-information PDF: 'Application fee: € 50.' EU citizens and citizens given parity of treatment (including a Turkish citizen holding an Italian work, family, asylum or religious residence permit) pay nothing to apply. The fee is separate from and additional to the €600 first instalment of tuition later used to secure the place, and it is not credited against tuition. There is no fee for applying to more than one session or more than one programme within the EU track. Note the asymmetry this creates for the non-EU cohort: €50 buys entry to a single annual window contesting 10 places against roughly 40 qualified competitors, with no reapplication route within the same year.
tuition_or_fees_link: €1,200 per academic year, in two instalments — among the lowest tuition levels of any public university in northern Italy, and identical for EU and non-EU students (unibz applies no international surcharge and does not use ISEE-based fee banding for this figure). Programme page and brochure: 'Tuition fees: ca. € 1200 per year'. Admission-information PDF: 'Fees amount to € 1200 — 1st instalment (€ 600): includes the revenue stamp of € 16. 2nd instalment (€ 600): must be paid by March of the following year.' The university-wide fees regulation (Study Guide, https://guide.unibz.it/en/study-career/general-information/fees/) gives the precise 2026/27 dates and the out-of-duration rates: within normal programme duration, 1st instalment €600 by 13 October 2026 and 2nd instalment €600 by 31 March 2027; beyond normal duration ('fuori corso'), the 1st instalment rises to €900 while the 2nd stays at €600. A €16 revenue stamp is payable by everyone, and a €30 fine applies to late payment. CONSEQUENCES OF NON-PAYMENT: 'If you have not paid the tuition fees, you will be unable to take exams and will not be able to transfer to other universities or other study programmes'; late payment also blocks access to mySNS and to exam registration. NO REFUNDS: 'If you drop out of a programme, interrupt your studies or are excluded from studies, you are not entitled to reimbursement of the fees' — the single exception being non-EU applicants abroad who do not obtain the documents necessary for enrolment from the Italian authorities. EXEMPTIONS: students with a disability recognised under art. 3(1) of Law 104/1992 or with an invalidity of 66% or more (certificate to be filed at the start of the academic year), and foreign students holding an Italian government scholarship — both pay only the €16 stamp. Students holding a scholarship from the Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano are reimbursed the fees, normally in March-April, though 'any fines due to late payment will not be reimbursed'. Budgeting note for a visa file: tuition is the small item — unibz itself tells non-EU applicants to plan on at least €800 per month of living costs on top.
scholarships_grants: THREE LAYERS, and the first is essentially unavailable to a newly arrived non-EU student. (1) PROVINCIAL NEED-BASED SCHOLARSHIP (Ufficio per il diritto allo studio universitario, Autonomous Province of Bozen-Bolzano) — 'students can apply for a scholarship... and they may be able to obtain - depending on their income - between €1,680 and €6,960 per year. If students have a right to a scholarship, they will also get a refund of the tuition fees.' The student associations sh.asus and MUA assist with the application. THE CATCH for internationals: unibz's own non-EU page states that non-EU residents cannot apply for provincial scholarships until after one year of regular registered residence in South Tyrol — so a Turkish student arriving for the first year must self-fund year one and can realistically only access this from year two. (2) MERIT SCHOLARSHIP — 'Those who, after the first year, get an average grade of 27/30 for their exams, are eligible to apply for scholarships based on merit rather than income.' This is the realistic first-year target for a strong international student, since it is keyed to performance rather than residence. (3) STATUTORY EXEMPTIONS AND REFUNDS — full fee exemption for students with a recognised disability of 66% or more and for holders of an Italian government scholarship; full fee reimbursement (paid March-April) for provincial scholarship holders. NO PROGRAMME-SPECIFIC SCHOLARSHIP is advertised for this master — the brochure and programme page mention none, and unlike some unibz programmes there is no industry-sponsored or faculty-funded award named for Data Analytics students, although the programme's PNRR/EDUNEXT co-funding supports teaching delivery rather than student stipends. Non-financial cost relief worth knowing: the südtirolmobil U26 Pass gives students under 26 a year of public transport across South Tyrol plus regional trains to Trento for €150; campus canteens are payable by Student Card; and private student halls (Pietro Tosolini Student Residence, Ferrari Tower, HIGHFIVEBZ) manage their own admissions and rents separately from the university.
credential_recognition: THREE COUNTRY-GROUP ROUTES, all executed at ENROLMENT rather than at application, and all resulting in a reservation on your admission until cleared. Base documents for any foreign degree: 'degree diploma of your Bachelor'; 'official translation of your degree into Italian (not necessary if the documents have been issued in German or English)'; and a 'Diploma supplement, where it must be indicated: that you have achieved at least 180 credit points (ECTS) and that the qualification gives access to a master programme'. THEN, by country group: (a) EU countries, Switzerland, Norway, Iceland, Liechtenstein — 'Statement of Correspondence of your Bachelor degree, to be downloaded from the ARDI - Automatic Recognition Database - Italy'. (b) Non-EU countries that ARE signatories to the Lisbon Convention — the ARDI Statement of Correspondence AND a 'Statement of Verification of your Bachelor degree, issued by the Italian Information Centre on Academic Mobility and Equivalence (CIMEA)'. (c) Non-EU countries that are NOT signatories of the Lisbon Convention — a CIMEA 'Statement of Comparability' AND a CIMEA 'Statement of Verification'. WHICH ROUTE APPLIES TO TÜRKIYE: Türkiye is a signatory to the Lisbon Recognition Convention, so route (b) applies — ARDI Statement of Correspondence plus CIMEA Statement of Verification. This is the cheaper and faster of the two non-EU routes because ARDI is a free public database lookup rather than a paid CIMEA assessment, and only the Verification (a genuineness check with the issuing university) has to be purchased; applicants should nonetheless allow several weeks for CIMEA processing and start well before the 13/10/2026 enrolment deadline. THE RESERVATION MECHANIC, verbatim from the ranking-list decrees: 'Your admission will be under reservation until the above-mentioned documents are uploaded. During enrolment, unibz verifies your foreign qualification and may request additional documents if necessary. If the access title is deemed eligible, the reservation will be lifted. Otherwise, enrolment will not be possible and you will be excluded.' And the long tail of risk: 'if you do not possess a valid admission qualification, you can be excluded with Rector's decree even after enrolment.' Note that at APPLICATION stage the requirements are lighter — a transcript or degree certificate in Italian, German or English suffices, with no ARDI/CIMEA paperwork needed to be ranked; only the diploma itself must be uploaded then if you already hold it.
non_eu_visa_process: A FIVE-STEP CHAIN WITH ONE IRREVERSIBLE CHOICE IN THE MIDDLE. (1) APPLY to unibz in the Early Bird window (02/03-28/04/2026) and pay the €50 non-refundable application fee. (2) IF ADMITTED, SECURE THE PLACE by paying the €600 first instalment by 05/06/2026 noon — this must happen BEFORE the visa step. (3) PRE-ENROL ON UNIVERSITALY, which is mandatory and singular: 'start your visa application on the Universitaly portal. The application on Universitaly is mandatory, otherwise you will not be allowed to enrol. On Universitaly you can apply for one study programme only.' unibz warns that failing to follow this procedure renders the direct application null and void. The one-programme restriction is the irreversible choice: whatever you select on Universitaly is the only degree the visa will support. (4) OBTAIN THE STUDY VISA from the Italian embassy or consulate in your country. unibz is explicit that this is outside its control: 'admission to unibz does not confer automatically any right to obtaining a visa', and conversely a visa confers no right to enrol. Proof of financial means for the visa: at least €800 per month of living costs in the Bozen-Bolzano area excluding tuition, and unibz states a total requirement of at least €24,000 for a master programme (versus at least €36,000 for a three-year bachelor); health insurance and visa expenses must be budgeted on top. The consulate sends an official communication directly to unibz, and until it arrives every non-EU admission stays provisional — 'All non-EU citizens living abroad are provisionally admitted: requirement is the official communication sent by the Italian consulate abroad directly to unibz.' (5) ON ARRIVAL, apply for the residence permit within 8 working days: 'According to Italian law, within 8 working days of your arrival in Italy, you must have applied for the residence permit: as soon as you arrive, get in touch with the Advisory Service and you will be given the necessary information for starting the procedure. Once you will obtain your residence permit (permesso di soggiorno), you have to hand it in at the Student Office personally or via e-mail.' Then enrol online by 13/10/2026 noon. WORK RIGHTS while studying: 20 hours a week and no more than 1,040 hours per year. PERMIT RENEWAL in later years requires evidence of funds — unibz cites an Italian bank statement showing at least €7,002.84. uncertainty_notes: WHAT IS SOLID: everything on places, dates, entry requirements, SSD lists, the scoring rubric, the 140-ECTS conditional threshold, fees, language rules and the credential-recognition chain comes from the 2026/27 admission-information PDF (updated 24.08.2026), the 2026/27 brochure, the programme page and the two digitally signed ranking-list decrees, which agree with each other throughout. The competition figures come straight from the signed decrees and are facts, not estimates. WHAT IS UNCERTAIN OR NEEDS A CAVEAT: (1) FIRST INTAKE YEAR. unibz never states when the programme started. The inference of a.y. 2023/24 rests on circumstantial evidence — the earliest Internet Archive capture of the programme page is 30/01/2023, the course-contents document is named and headed for 2023, and unibz promoted the programme on LinkedIn in February 2023. web.archive.org could not be fetched directly to confirm, so this remains an inference. (2) EXIT LANGUAGE LEVEL. The finding of 'no exit language requirement' is derived from silence: the admission-information PDF has an entry-level section and no exit-level section, whereas unibz's trilingual programmes have both. A study regulation published only in Italian or German could in principle say otherwise; confirm with the Faculty Secretariat if it matters. (3) THIRD-LANGUAGE B1. Recorded as not applicable on the same absence-of-evidence basis. (4) NO ENGLISH-LANGUAGE BANDO. The claim that no separate call/manifesto exists cannot be proved exhaustively; an Italian-language administrative act may sit in unibz's Albo online. (5) THE LATE-SESSION OVER-ADMISSION. Twenty EU applicants were admitted in a session with a nominal quota of 10. The explanation offered — early-bird places freed by non-confirming admits rolling over, as the roll-over rule permits — is a reading of the two decrees together, not something unibz states. (6) FACULTY ATTRIBUTION. The programme lives on an Economics and Management URL and is administered by that faculty's secretariat, yet the Faculty of Engineering lists it in its own study-programme menu and the Additional Application Session page lists it under both faculties. The cross-listing is a documented fact; whether unibz formally designates it an inter-faculty degree is not stated in English. (7) ADDITIONAL-SESSION OUTCOME UNKNOWN. As of 2026-08-29 the third window was still open (closes 04/09/2026 noon) and its ranking list, due by 18/09/2026, did not exist yet — so the final 2026/27 intake size and the additional session's cut-off score are not knowable from this snapshot. (8) DOCUMENT DEFECTS THAT COULD MISLEAD A CAREFUL READER: the Early Bird decree prints 'max. 90 88 points'; the dual-enrolment rule is illustrated with 'LM-63/LM-63' in the admission PDF and 'LM-18/LM-18' in the decrees, neither of which is this programme's class; and the Early Bird ranking-list filename misspells 'Managment'. (9) VOLATILITY. Dates, quotas and cut-off scores change every admission cycle; the 2027/28 figures will differ and the admission PDF is explicitly 'subject to change'. (10) CORRECTION TO THE RESEARCH BRIEF: the working note described the 140-ECTS conditional threshold as this programme's peculiarity against a 120 standard. That is only half right — 140 is the Faculty of Economics and Management's uniform threshold (Accounting and Finance, Entrepreneurship and Innovation and Public Policy all use it); the 120 figure is the Engineering-side norm. The brief also dated LM-Data to 'after 2024'; the class was in fact created by MUR Decree no. 146 of 09/02/2021, with Italian universities enrolling into it from 2022/23.
